# The Pursuit of Power

## Technology, Armed Force, and Society since A.D. 1000

[William H. McNeill](https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/author/M/W/au5371842.html)

In this magnificent synthesis of military, technological, and social history, William H. McNeill explores a whole millennium of human upheaval and traces the path by which we have arrived at the frightening dilemmas that now confront us.

...

Only in our own time, suggests McNeill, are command economies replacing the market control of large-scale human effort. The Pursuit of Power does not solve the problems of the present, but its discoveries, hypotheses, and sheer breadth of learning do offer a perspective on our current fears and, as McNeill hopes, "a ground for wiser action."

For the historian, the task of reviewing a book by the redoubtable William McNeill is a mixed blessing. On the one hand, the assignment bespeaks a certain confidence—or rashness—on the part of the editor responsible.
